subject: Literacy
title: Strong fingers
objectives: Children will squeeze, pinch and poke playdough and sponges.
Children will thread large objects with support.
content: Squeezing and pinching playdough and sponges, threading large beads, and finger games.
teachingActivities: Show each movement slowly and let children feel it; work at a table with the children sitting comfortably; use big, soft materials; celebrate effort over neatness.
learnerActivities: Squeeze, pinch, poke and roll playdough and sponges, and thread large beads with support.
resources: Thick string with a stiff end
assessment: Observe whether each child squeezes and rolls playdough and threads at least one large bead.
expectedOutcomes: Threads at least one large bead.

lessons.title: Squeeze and pinch
lessons.subject: Literacy
objectives: Children will squeeze and pinch playdough with their fingers.
successCriteria: Squeezes playdough with the whole hand
lessons.previousKnowledge: Children can clap beats, do finger rhymes and hold a book; many are still developing hand strength.
lessons.starter: Hold a ball of playdough and say "Squeeze, squeeze, squeeze." Show a pinch and say "Pinch, pinch."
teacherActivities: Squeeze the playdough in your fist and say "Squeeze". Show it to the children.
Pinch a small piece with your thumb and finger and say "Pinch".
Say "Squeeze" and "Pinch" in turn and wait.
Let each child make a squashed shape and show a friend.
presentation: Step 1. Teacher: Squeeze the playdough in your fist and say "Squeeze". Show it to the children. Children: Children squeeze their own piece.
Step 2. Teacher: Pinch a small piece with your thumb and finger and say "Pinch". Children: Children pinch with their fingers.
Step 3. Teacher: Say "Squeeze" and "Pinch" in turn and wait. Children: Children change their action.
Step 4. Teacher: Let each child make a squashed shape and show a friend. Children: Child shows their shape.

practical.title: Playdough time
steps: Give each child a tray and a ball of playdough.
Make a shape and show a friend.
practical.safety: Use non-toxic playdough and check for allergies. Do not let children eat it. Wash hands before and after.

differentiation.support: Squeeze the dough together with a hand over the child’s hand.
differentiation.extension: Ask the child to pinch five small pieces.

assessment.method: Observe each child during the practical activity and note Emerging, Developing, Secure or Exceeding on the class record. Ask the questions below one to one or in a small group.

expectedOutcomes: Names the actions squeeze and pinch
lessons.conclusion: Put the playdough away and wash hands.
lessons.homeConnection: Let your child squeeze and pinch bread dough or soft clay with you.
teacherReflection: Which children could show "squeeze and pinch playdough with their fingers" without help, and who needs another turn tomorrow?
What did the children say or do that I did not expect, and how will I use it in the next lesson?
Which resource or instruction worked best, and what would I change before I teach this again?

learnerFacing.songOrRhyme: Squeeze, squeeze, squeeze it. Pinch, pinch, pinch it.

lessons.title: Roll and poke
lessons.subject: Literacy
objectives: Children will roll and poke playdough to make shapes.
successCriteria: Rolls dough into a ball or a snake
lessons.previousKnowledge: Children can clap beats, do finger rhymes and hold a book; many are still developing hand strength.
lessons.starter: Roll a ball of playdough in your palms and say "Roll, roll, roll." Poke a hole and say "Poke."
teacherActivities: Roll a ball between your hands. Then roll a long snake on the tray.
Poke the ball with one finger to make a hole.
Let each child make something and name it.
learnerActivities: Children copy rolling a ball and a snake.
Child shows their shape and names it.
presentation: Step 1. Teacher: Roll a ball between your hands. Then roll a long snake on the tray. Children: Children copy rolling a ball and a snake.
Step 2. Teacher: Poke the ball with one finger to make a hole. Children: Children poke their balls.
Step 3. Teacher: Say "Roll", "Poke", "Squeeze" in turn and wait. Children: Children do each action.
Step 4. Teacher: Let each child make something and name it. Children: Child shows their shape and names it.

practical.title: Dough shapes
steps: Give each child a tray and dough.
Roll a ball and a snake.
Poke holes and make a shape.
practical.safety: Use only non-toxic dough and keep it off the face. Wash hands after play and wipe the trays.

differentiation.support: Roll the dough together and poke with the child’s finger.
differentiation.extension: Ask the child to make a snake and curl it into a circle.

assessment.method: Observe each child during the practical activity and note Emerging, Developing, Secure or Exceeding on the class record. Ask the questions below one to one or in a small group.

expectedOutcomes: Rolls playdough into a ball or snake
lessons.conclusion: Pack the dough into a box and say goodbye.
lessons.homeConnection: Roll and poke dough or mud at home with your child.
teacherReflection: Which children could show "roll and poke playdough to make shapes" without help, and who needs another turn tomorrow?
What did the children say or do that I did not expect, and how will I use it in the next lesson?
Which resource or instruction worked best, and what would I change before I teach this again?

lessons.title: Sponge squeezing
lessons.subject: Literacy
objectives: Children will squeeze a sponge to move water from one bowl to another.
successCriteria: Squeezes a sponge with the whole hand
lessons.previousKnowledge: Children can clap beats, do finger rhymes and hold a book; many are still developing hand strength.
lessons.starter: Dip a sponge in water and squeeze it over the bowl. Say "Squeeze, squeeze. Drip, drip."
teacherActivities: Show how to squeeze the sponge so water drips into the bowl.
Let each child dip a sponge and squeeze it into the empty bowl.
Count how many squeezes it takes to fill a small bowl.
learnerActivities: Child squeezes and watches the water.
Children squeeze and count with you.
presentation: Step 1. Teacher: Show how to squeeze the sponge so water drips into the bowl. Children: Children watch and say "drip".
Step 2. Teacher: Let each child dip a sponge and squeeze it into the empty bowl. Children: Child squeezes and watches the water.
Step 3. Teacher: Say "Squeeze hard" and "Squeeze softly". Children: Children change how they squeeze.
Step 4. Teacher: Count how many squeezes it takes to fill a small bowl. Children: Children squeeze and count with you.

practical.title: Water squeeze
steps: Set up two bowls on a tray with sponges.
Squeeze water from one bowl to the other.
practical.safety: Keep water shallow and supervise at all times. Wipe spills quickly and use a towel under the tray.

differentiation.support: Use a small sponge and squeeze together.
differentiation.extension: Ask the child to move all the water to the other bowl.

assessment.method: Observe each child during the practical activity and note Emerging, Developing, Secure or Exceeding on the class record. Ask the questions below one to one or in a small group.

questions.question: What do we do with the sponge?

expectedOutcomes: Moves water from one bowl to another
lessons.conclusion: Wring the sponges and put them on the tray to dry.
lessons.homeConnection: Let your child squeeze a sponge in the bath or at the sink.
teacherReflection: Which children could show "squeeze a sponge to move water from one bowl to another" without help, and who needs another turn tomorrow?
What did the children say or do that I did not expect, and how will I use it in the next lesson?
Which resource or instruction worked best, and what would I change before I teach this again?

lessons.title: Threading beads
lessons.subject: Literacy
objectives: Children will thread a large bead onto a string with support.
successCriteria: Holds a string and a bead
Pushes a string through a bead
lessons.previousKnowledge: Children can clap beats, do finger rhymes and hold a book; many are still developing hand strength.
resources: Thick strings with a stiff end
lessons.starter: Hold up a bead and a string and say "We thread the bead on the string. Push it through."
teacherActivities: Show how to hold the bead in one hand and push the string through with the other.
Help each child thread one bead and pull it down the string.
Ask the child to thread a second bead.
Show the beads to a friend.
learnerActivities: Children watch and hold a bead.
Child threads a bead with support.
presentation: Step 1. Teacher: Show how to hold the bead in one hand and push the string through with the other. Children: Children watch and hold a bead.
Step 2. Teacher: Help each child thread one bead and pull it down the string. Children: Child threads a bead with support.
Step 3. Teacher: Ask the child to thread a second bead. Children: Child threads two beads.
Step 4. Teacher: Show the beads to a friend. Children: Child shows and says "bead".

practical.title: Bead threading
steps: Give each child a tray with large beads and a string.
Count the beads together at the end.
practical.safety: Use only beads larger than a child’s fist-sized opening so they cannot be swallowed. Supervise closely and put a knot at the end of each string.

differentiation.support: Hold the bead and let the child push the string through.
differentiation.extension: Ask the child to thread five beads in a pattern.

assessment.method: Observe each child during the practical activity and note Emerging, Developing, Secure or Exceeding on the class record. Ask the questions below one to one or in a small group.

expectedOutcomes: Threads at least one large bead with support
lessons.conclusion: Count the beads and put them in a bowl.
lessons.homeConnection: Thread large pasta tubes onto string with your child under supervision.
teacherReflection: Which children could show "thread a large bead onto a string with support" without help, and who needs another turn tomorrow?
What did the children say or do that I did not expect, and how will I use it in the next lesson?
Which resource or instruction worked best, and what would I change before I teach this again?

lessons.title: Week 3 fingers check
lessons.subject: Literacy
objectives: Teachers will observe how each child uses their fingers to squeeze, roll and thread.
lessons.previousKnowledge: Children can clap beats, do finger rhymes and hold a book; many are still developing hand strength.
lessons.starter: Sing "Squeeze, squeeze, squeeze it" and show three stations.
teacherActivities: Set up three stations: playdough, sponge squeezing and bead threading.
Watch each child and note how they squeeze, roll and thread.
Record each child’s level and take photographs.
learnerActivities: Children wash hands and tidy at the signal.
presentation: Step 1. Teacher: Set up three stations: playdough, sponge squeezing and bead threading. Children: Children rotate every five minutes.
Step 2. Teacher: Watch each child and note how they squeeze, roll and thread. Children: Children play at each station.
Step 3. Teacher: Record each child’s level and take photographs. Children: Children wash hands and tidy at the signal.

practical.title: Finger stations
practical.safety: Supervise beads and water closely. Use non-toxic dough and wash hands after each station.

differentiation.support: Provide an adult partner and offer one station to start.
differentiation.extension: Ask a confident child to teach a friend how to thread.

assessment.method: Observe and record Emerging, Developing, Secure or Exceeding for: squeezes playdough; rolls dough; threads at least one large bead.

expectedOutcomes: Has an observation record for Week 3
lessons.homeConnection: Play with dough or clay at home and let your child squeeze and roll.
teacherReflection: Which children could show "Teachers will observe how each child uses their fingers to squeeze, roll and thread" without help, and who needs another turn tomorrow?
What did the children say or do that I did not expect, and how will I use it in the next lesson?
Which resource or instruction worked best, and what would I change before I teach this again?
